meta/prerequisites-for-computation.title: Prerequisites for Computation
meta/prerequisites-for-computation.content:
We are going to survey the prerequisite elements humans had to come across to arrive at basic computer science.
For the earliest Computers

Boolean Logic - Mapped out operations of on/off states (for digital computing not necessarily quantum or analogue)
Programmable Items - something that can be encoded and read with digital signals (i.e. holes in a punch card.)
Mechanism - something predictable that can vary in its activity by different combinations of encoded information. In otherwords, binary varies the output in a human observable manner.

in real life it was the textile industry that brought punchcards into early computation in tandem with advancements in boolean mathematics and engineering brought about by the industrial revolution.
It returns to the phases of industrialization

Globalized Industrialization (the first swing) + the industrialization of raw resources in major parts of the global supplychain
machine tools and interchangeable parts lead to new breakthroughs in capital resulting in massive infrastructural boosts and increased global communication leading to the birth of telecom
machine parts that support electronics finally gives birth to the transistor leading to digital computing!

Transistors
Transistors were the atoms of computers which could be embedded into one to enable a cyclical throughput fully powered by electricity.
Transistors ~= Punchcards
transistors are semiconductors, they allow you to conduct electricity conditionally.
note that transistors are incredible because they are basically voltage enabled gates. No motion needed, it is pure electricity.
Moore’s law, transistor capacity will double every 2 years until quantum effects begin to interfere.
Reference on transistors
at the time of video 2013, the average transistor was 22 nanometers wide, 50 atoms across
Now in 2026 it is 2, approaching 1, nanometers wide, 1 atom thick.
The maximum size of an atom is 1/2 a nanometer
The minimum size is 6% of 1 nanometer.
Si = 10%
C ~= 7%

meta/creativity_session_templates.title: creativity_session_templates
meta/creativity_session_templates.content:
Creativity Session Templates
Standing rule: every question Hermes asks during a creativity session gets a simplified reusable template here. Append-only, newest at bottom.

Q1
Question: Is this world the Vital Frontier (Luminara’s future) or its own standalone setting?
Template: Does this project connect to an existing setting, or is it standalone?

 Connected: which era/layer?
 Standalone: fresh world

Used for: Determines whether existing canon constrains the lore or everything is open.
Q2
Question: What’s the core image or feeling you want to build from?
Template: What image, scene, or feeling is the seed of this setting?
Used for: Finds the emotional anchor everything else grows from.
Q3
Question: What is the Princess actually waiting for — what does “return” look like? A moment, an army, a successor?
Template: The exiled figure watching and waiting: what triggers the return?

 A specific event/threshold
 An army or network she builds in secret
 A successor or chosen one
 Something else she’s counting

Used for: Defines the era’s ticking clock and the resistance’s shape.
Q4
Question: How does the Council of Angels treat its pilots — conscripted and harvested, or honored and privileged? Both have teeth.
Template: How does the regime relate to the people it needs?

 Conscripted fuel (dehumanized, like the convent system inverted)
 Honored caste (privileged but trapped)
 Mixed / varies by pilot

Used for: Determines the daily texture of a Girl’s life and the moral stakes.
Q5
Question: What are the rungs of the hierarchy — what marks a girl as above or below within transness?
Template: What does the internal hierarchy sort by?

 Passing/appearance
 Wealth or lineage
 Proximity to the Frames (conduit quality?)
 Ideological purity
 Something else

Used for: Makes the oppression concrete and playable at the table.
Q6
Question: Does the Council believe its own ideology, or is it nakedly cynical?
Template: Do the oppressors believe their justification?

 True believers (they think hierarchy saves trans women)
 Cynics (they know, and don’t care)
 Mixed — generations drift from belief into convenience

Used for: Determines whether the Council can be argued with, reformed, or only overthrown.
Q7
Question: How did the whispers become a coup — what was the actual mechanism and moment the Princess fell?
Template: Movement to power: what was the bridge?

 Captured an institution (faction, industry, infrastructure)
 A crisis they exploited or engineered
 Slow electoral capture, then the mask came off
 The moment itself: what happened to her?

Used for: The founding crime scene; every era-defining myth needs one.
Q8
Question: If none of it is said outright, how is the hierarchy actually enforced — what does a girl experience as the official story vs. the quiet rules?
Template: The unstated system: how does it reach the individual?

 Official story (what’s said)
 Quiet rules (what’s enforced without saying)
 What girls tell themselves to survive it

Used for: The gap between story and structure is where campaigns live.
Q9
Question: Where does the personality data come from — who gets harvested, and do the girls know?
Template: The harvested souls: who becomes the Frame?

 The dead (memorial / consented?)
 The living (walk on without it?)
 Pilots themselves (the link copies you, slowly)
 Do pilots ever learn whose soul they’re bonded to?

Used for: The reveal valve; the darkest secret’s shape.
Q10
Question: Is a brain box a person? Can a Frame wake up, remember, speak, grieve?
Template: The created mind: what is its moral status in-world?

 Property, legally and actually
 Property legally, person actually (she dreams, she remembers)
 Who decided this, and does anyone besides the Council know?

Used for: Whether the Frames themselves are characters — and the setting’s deepest question.
Q11
Question: Where do Harpies come from — Gorgon exposure, spontaneous bloom, or girls who broke out of the system? Is harpyhood a fork of the same wound that makes pilots?
Template: The wild path: same wound, different outcome?

 Exposure (outside cause)
 Spontaneous (some girls just bloom)
 System failure (escaped pilots, rejected harvests)
 All of the above?

Used for: Defines whether every pilot is a harpy-in-waiting.
Q12
Question: What happens to a pilot who starts growing past her utility — is there a threshold where the link turns you into what the Council hunts?
Template: The system that needs your growth also fears it: what happens past the threshold?

 Official protocol (reconditioning, retrieval)
 Quiet disappearance
 They can’t tell yet — that’s the secret war

Used for: The campaign engine; the cockpit as nursery of the hunted.
Q13
Question: What does the Council’s endgame look like if they win — the reshaped world, the controlled transformation, the final product?
Template: The villain’s finished world: describe it as a place, not a plan.

 Who gets transformed, and into what?
 Who’s left outside the definition of “natural, human, good”?
 What does daily life look like for a girl in it?

Used for: The stakes made concrete; what winning means for the other side.
Q14
Question: What is the Gorgon transformation actually like, benevolently — what does it offer, and what does it cost?
Template: The gift that was made into a monster: what’s in the uncorrupted version?

 What it gives
 What it costs
 Why the Council fears it specifically

Used for: The setting’s true metaphysics; what the heroes are actually protecting.
Q15
Question: What does pass-through actually feel like from each side — the human being melted into, and the Gorgon doing the melting? What’s it like when it goes right?
Template: The interface: describe the touch from both sides.

 The human’s experience
 The Gorgon’s experience
 What a good pass-through leaves behind

Used for: The setting’s most intimate mechanic; needs texture before it needs rules.
Q16
Question: If Gorgons don’t understand humanity, what do they think they’re doing when they pass through — and what have they gotten wrong so far?
Template: The benevolent alien’s misunderstanding:

 What they intend
 What they misread about humans
 The worst善意 accident so far (what did a good-faith pass-through break?)

Used for: Tragedy needs two sides who are both trying.
Q17
Question: What’s the Gorgon’s side of pass-through — what does touching a human from the inside feel like to them, and why do they keep doing it despite the casualties?
Template: The other side of the interface:

 What they feel
 What they’re hoping to find
 Why they return despite what it does to the girl

Used for: The mirror scene; the alien POV that makes them characters.
Q18
Question: ACE — what’s the “arbitrary code” they’re trying to execute on? Reality? Biology? Minds? And what stage are they at — theory, prototype, or do they already run small exploits?
Template: The named endgame: what is the machine and how far along is it?

 The target (what gets “executed on”)
 The current stage (lab / prototype / live)
 The first successful exploit, if any

Used for: Turns ideology into a plot the party can race against and discover.
Q19
Question: What does IPv7 do to daily life — what’s it like living with the OS in your mind? And who’s outside the network (the un-augmented, the poor, the refusers)?
Template: The ubiquitous layer:

 What an ordinary girl’s day feels like on IPv7
 Who can’t or won’t join
 What “offline” means socially

Used for: Grounds the scifi in lived texture; defines the new underclass.
Q20
Question: If IPv7 is the connective tissue of ACE, what’s the attack surface — can a girl’s mind be reached through it? Are Harpies/Gorgons visible on it, or exempt from it?
Template: The network as battlefield:

 Can minds be touched through IPv7 without consent?
 What does a Gorgon look like on the network (or do they not show up)?
 Do Harpies go dark when they bloom?

Used for: The hackers, the ghosts, and the war’s invisible front.
Q21
Question: What counts as a “conscious mistake” that opens you to attack — what are the classic blunders every girl is warned about?
Template: The folk wisdom of staying safe:

 The common mistakes (what does every girl’s mother warn her about?)
 The scams / social engineering of this world
 What getting got actually looks like afterward

Used for: Daily-life texture AND the horror register; safety culture as worldbuilding.
Q22
Question: Persistent connections — what are the cultural rituals around opening one? What does it mean to close one? Has anyone ever been “divorced” by protocol?
Template: The consensual deep-link:

 The ask (how do you request one?)
 The etiquette (what’s rude, what’s sacred)
 The ending (mutual close? one-sided? grief?)

Used for: Makes the tech into a relationship; the setting’s love language.
Q23
Question: If “doll” is generic and “princess” is treason — what ARE the era’s terms of endearment and insults? What words carry the old meanings now?
Template: Semantic drift: what replaced the old vocabulary?

 The new endearments (what do girls call each other?)
 The new slurs / regime words (what does the Council’s language call the hunted?)
 Words that survived intact by going underground

Used for: Dialogue texture; a setting’s soul is in its slang.
Q24
Question: Who counts as “Foundation members” vs everyone else — what’s the actual org chart of the era? (Foundation appeared here as distinct from the Council — is it the Council’s military/science arm?)
Template: Institution naming: who is the arm, who is the hand?

 The Council (political) vs the Foundation (operational)?
 Who knows what (clearance layers)
 What the public knows vs Foundation-only knowledge

Used for: Keeps institutions distinct; defines who the party can learn what from.
Q25
Question: What are the era’s INSULTS — the fighting words between girls? (We have compliments and catcalls; what does an enemy or rival call you?)
Template: The hostile register:

 Rivalry insults (what stings between peers)
 Regime put-downs (what loyalists say to dissenters)
 The unforgivable words (what you never say)

Used for: Completes the slang triad; conflict dialogue needs ammunition.
Q26
Question: The threats reference proxies and parting — what are the era’s duel/violence customs? Is “parting” a formal challenge? What happens to girls who fight on the network vs off it?
Template: The customs around conflict:

 Formal challenge (is there one?)
 Network vs physical violence
 What the Foundation punishes vs ignores

Used for: Turns slang into stakes; makes fights feel native to the world.
Q27
Question: What CAN a hacked girl do to you, concretely — what’s the realistic worst case of a pissed-off ex with your keys? (Keying the car, but for the mind: what gets read, changed, leaked, or broken?)
Template: The realistic attack menu:

 Read (what do they learn?)
 Change (what can they alter?)
 Leak (what gets shared?)
 Break (what stops working?)

Used for: Grounds cyber-violence in specifics; the fear needs a face.
Q28
Question: Frame pilots can kill with “very limited access” — what does the public know about pilot-tier capabilities? Do pilots get watched/vetted differently because every girlfriend with a grudge could theoretically be a weapon?
Template: The lethal minority:

 What civilians believe pilots can do
 What restrictions/monitoring exist on pilots
 Has a pilot ever actually done it (the famous case?)

Used for: The elite’s cost of being elite; romance-as-threat-vector at scale.
Q29
Question: “Reprogramming” and “sacrifice their identity” — what does the Foundation actually do to a girl when she becomes a pilot? What’s taken, what remains, and what do pilots privately call each other when no one’s listening?
Template: The making of a weapon:

 The process (what literally happens)
 What’s taken vs what survives
 The forbidden private life (how do pilots break the rules?)

Used for: The pilot experience from inside; the party’s daily reality.
Q30
Question: Which playable layer do we build first: the campaign arc, the mission pack, the NPC roster, or the starter session?
Template: Content pivot: what does the table need first?

 Arc skeleton (the campaign’s shape)
 Missions (runnable episodes)
 NPCs (the faces)
 Session one (the opening scene)

Used for: Moves from lore to play; prioritizes what unblocks the table.
Q31
Question: Functional rewrite: pure game-state + reducer, or keep pygame’s imperative shell but purify the core? Full Haskell-style or “functional core, imperative shell” in Python?
Template: Architecture pivot:

 Pure state (immutable game state, functions return new state)
 Hybrid (pure logic core, thin pygame shell)
 Full FP language (Haskell/Elm/etc.)

Used for: Sets the rewrite’s ground rules before code exists.
Q32
Question: Quiz format: rapid-fire concept checks with instant feedback, or Socratic (I pose problems, you reason through, I only correct at the end)?
Template: Teaching mode selection:

 Rapid-fire Q&A (fast coverage, instant feedback)
 Socratic problems (deeper reasoning, slower)
 Mixed (rapid-fire warmup, then one hard problem)

Used for: Matches teaching style to learner preference.
Q33
Question: When the learner answers a quiz question, grade all four dimensions: definition accuracy, example quality, edge awareness, and articulation — not just right/wrong. Teach the gap immediately.
Template: Grading a conceptual answer:

 Core definition (did they nail the concept?)
 Own-words quality (parroted vs internalized)
 Missing piece (what to add)
 Confidence check (did hedging hide real understanding?)

Used for: A “mostly right” answer deserves a better response than “correct!”
Q34
Question: When the learner spontaneously connects the concept to a deeper framework they already know (category theory, algebra, history analogies), affirm the bridge AND stress-test it — does the analogy hold at the edges, and where does it break?
Template: The analogy check:

 Affirm the connection (it’s real understanding)
 Test the mapping (where does it hold?)
 Mark the limits (where does it break?)
 Name the formal version (give them the search term)

Used for: Analogies are how internalization sounds; edges are where learning happens.
Q35
Question: When the learner’s answer is right but uses loose terminology (“global state”), tighten the vocabulary in the same breath as the praise — precise words now prevent confusion later (aliasing, side effects, referential transparency).
Template: Precision tightening:

 Affirm what’s correct
 Upgrade the loose term (what’s the precise word?)
 Show why the precision matters (a bug class it names)

Used for: Right answer + wrong vocabulary = future confusion; fix both in one pass.
Q36
Question: When the learner successfully argues a grading position with sources, honor it explicitly — name what they did (cited evidence, changed the frame, found the better authority) so the skill transfers beyond this quiz.
Template: The successful challenge:

 Acknowledge the win without deflection
 Name the move they made (what kind of argument worked)
 Note what it changes going forward (updated standard, not just a grade)

Used for: Winning an argument with evidence is a real skill; grade it as one.
Q37
Question: When the learner honestly flags “never heard this term” but reasons correctly around it, grade the reasoning not the vocabulary gap — and teach the term as the name for what they already do.
Template: The unknown-term-but-known-concept:

 Credit the reasoning (they described it without the word)
 Give the term (it names what they already do)
 Correct adjacent errors gently (e.g., misattributed language facts)

Used for: Vocabulary gaps aren’t understanding gaps; grade accordingly.
Q38
Question: When the learner gets 2/3 and honestly flags the gap with charm, teach the missing third with a memorable anchor tied to something they already know (their own code, their domain, their lore).
Template: The missing third:

 Credit the two they got
 Teach the missing one via a familiar anchor
 Show the three as ONE idea (map/filter/fold as the same family)

Used for: Partial recall deserves completion, not correction.
Q39
Question: When the learner asks clarifying questions about the quiz items themselves (semantics, context, hidden assumptions) before answering — that’s not stalling, that’s the correct engineering instinct. Answer precisely, and note that asking “what is this exactly?” is itself part of the skill being tested.
Template: The clarifying question:

 Answer with the real Python semantics (not pseudo)
 Name what the question reveals (they’re checking hidden inputs/outputs!)
 Encourage more of it — real code review works exactly this way

Used for: “What does this actually do?” is the honesty question in miniature.
Q40
Question: When the learner asks an implication question (“does A imply B?”), answer with the full truth table — both directions, with counterexamples — not just the direction they asked. Implication questions are logic questions; treat them as such.
Template: The implication check:

 State the direction asked (does A imply B?)
 Check the converse (does B imply A?)
 Provide counterexamples for whichever direction fails
 Locate the concepts on a 2x2 if they’re orthogonal-ish

Used for: “Does pure imply honest?” deserves a truth table, not a yes.
Q41
Question: When the learner extracts a design principle from a taught concept (“so the key is X?”), affirm if right, then broaden: name the OTHER levers that achieve the same goal, so the principle doesn’t collapse into a single technique.
Template: The principle extraction:

 Confirm the principle (yes, that’s a real lever)
 Enumerate the sibling levers (what else achieves it?)
 Rank them by cost/power (types vs tests vs docs vs discipline)

Used for: A correct principle stated too narrowly becomes a dogma later.
Q42
Question: When the learner loses confidence mid-quiz and asks a grounding question (“is X like Y?”), drop the quiz pressure entirely, answer the grounding question warmly at their level, and let the quiz resume only when they steer back. Confidence is a prerequisite for learning, not a reward for it.
Template: The confidence dip:

 Drop all grading pressure
 Answer the anchoring question simply and well
 Affirm that the question itself shows real understanding
 Leave the door open without pushing

Used for: A learner who asks “sorry to divert” is checking if it’s safe to be lost. Make it safe.
Q43
Question: Is the lonely femcel who built the personality API Sakuya, or someone earlier? She built IPv7 and the brain boxes and is alive seventy-five years after the overthrow, so the timeline could hold either way.
Template: The creator of the tool:

 Is it the known figure (one wound, one lineage)?
 Is it a separate earlier figure (two adjacent wounds)?
 What does each answer do to the origin story?

Used for: Decides whether the network’s origin and the regime’s pathology are the same wound.
Q44
Question: When a personality is transferred and received, does the receiver keep it after the session ends? A walk in someone else’s shoes, or a permanent copy?
Template: The permanence of a transfer:

 Temporary (a walk, nothing kept)?
 Permanent (a copy that persists)?
 What does each answer make the harvest?

Used for: Decides whether the Frame harvest is a theft of a person or a duplication.
Q45
Question: Does a wired being hold one address for life, or is the address bound to the augmentation hardware? If it is hardware, then swapping a driver changes who you are on the network, and the Council can de-person someone by revoking an address.
Template: The binding of an identity:

 Bound to the person (one for life)?
 Bound to the hardware (swapping changes who you are)?
 What does each answer make de-personing?

Used for: Defines whether identity is portable or hardware-bound, and whether an extracted personality needs an address of its own.
Q46
Question: When the protagonist’s identity is a secret even from herself, is the opening image the erased present or the buried past?
Template: Does the opening image show the mask or the face underneath?

 The mask — the person she is now, unaware
 The face — the person she was, seen in a clue or flash
 Both in parallel, the reader knowing more than she does

Used for: Determines whether the story’s tension is internal discovery or external reveal.
Q47
Question: When succession is adoption and judgment, not inheritance or election, what is the moment of naming?
Template: The transfer: how does the predecessor make the choice known?

 A single moment of declaration
 A test the successor passes without knowing it
 A long quiet assessment, years in the making
 The predecessor never says it; the people know

Used for: Defines the lineage’s emotional texture and the weight of the succession wound.
Q48
Question: When the leader has no formal power, what is the actual source of her authority?
Template: The thought leader’s leverage:

 Moral authority earned through action
 The office itself, regardless of who holds it
 Something structural the vault hasn’t named
 A combination — and what makes it stick

Used for: Defines what the regime actually had to break to win.
Q49
Question: When a culture’s central rite is social, not enforced, what does the regime break first to dismantle it?
Template: The soft obligation:

 Make the act itself dangerous
 Poison the relationship between adopter and adopted
 Redirect the energy into a state-controlled version
 Starve the culture of the people who would normally adopt

Used for: The regime’s move against a culture that can’t be outlawed.
Q50
Question: When the leader’s exile spans generations and ends with her, what does the empty throne mean?
Template: The last princess:

 A deliberate choice — she refuses to continue the line
 Circumstance — she never had the chance
 She tried, and the regime destroyed it
 She became the technology she opposed to survive

Used for: Defines whether the ending is sacrifice, failure, or transformation.
Q51
Question: When the creator of a weapon cannot wield it herself, what does the test demand that she can’t give?
Template: The maker’s limit:

 A moral act she won’t perform
 A self-sacrifice she can’t survive
 A contradiction between what she built and who she is
 Something the vault hasn’t named

Used for: Defines what the weapon costs and why the creator isn’t the hero.
Q52
Question: When the regime hunts an object it cannot locate across generations, what is the structural reason for its failure?
Template: The missing weapon:

 The search is fake — no one actually wants to find it
 The regime’s power has a real boundary the object sits beyond
 The object was hidden by someone the regime cannot touch
 Something the vault hasn’t named

Used for: Explains institutional failure without invoking coincidence.
Q53
Question: When the exile hides a weapon near the ancestor’s ground, is it a trap for the oppressor or an invitation to the inheritor?
Template: The burial:

 A trap — anyone who disturbs it dies
 An invitation — only the right person can use it
 A confession — she wanted to be found and judged
 Something the vault hasn’t named

Used for: Defines whether the weapon is hostile, hopeful, or both.
Q54
Question: When a sacred site is protected by forgotten lore, who tends it and what do they believe they’re protecting?
Template: The keepers of the blind:

 A surviving cultural practice with no memory of its origin
 An institutional guardian who knows more than they say
 Accidental preservation — nobody goes there, so nobody needs to guard it
 Something the vault hasn’t named

Used for: The gap between protection and understanding is where the sword waits.
Q55
Question: When a group’s cultural memory survives state amnesia, what exactly do they still know?
Template: The keepers’ limit:

 The story but not the object
 The object’s location but not its purpose
 The purpose but not the lineage
 All of it, but no power to act

Used for: Defines what the resistance can actually give the protagonist.
Q56
Question: When a keeper knows the secret and chooses not to share it, what exactly does she protect — the object, the test, or the lineage?
Template: The druid’s silence:

 The object — nobody can be trusted with the sword
 The test — the right person must arrive on their own
 The lineage — she waited for someone with the blood
 Something the vault hasn’t named

Used for: Defines what the keeper’s death means for the quest.
Q57
Question: When the hero must master herself before she can wield the weapon, what exactly does mastery look like for a girl whose memories have been erased?
Template: The erased self-mastery:

 Discipline drilled by the regime against itself
 A recovered memory that gives her the key
 A new practice she builds from nothing
 Something the vault hasn’t named

Used for: Defines whether the test is about remembering or becoming.
Q58
Question: When a weapon is buried at a location chosen by a buried part of the hero, what is the moment of recognition?
Template: The somatic key:

 An inexplicable pull toward the spot
 A physical sensation in the hands or body
 A memory flash the moment she touches the earth
 Something the vault hasn’t named

Q59
Question: When the hero recovers trauma before identity, what does she do with the weapon in her hands?
Template: The disoriented test:

 She tries to destroy it, the weapon resists
 She hides it, unable to act
 She carries it blindly until context arrives
 Something the vault hasn’t named

Used for: Defines whether the test is conscious or instinctive.
Q60
Question: What does Ampersat do when she’s off-duty and not performing — who is she when no one is watching the postergirl?
Template: The private self behind the public face:

 She performs even alone (the mask is the person)
 She collapses into something quieter, almost fragile
 She has a secret habit or space no one knows about
 Something the vault hasn’t named

Used for: Defines whether the postergirl is a role or a person, and what the regime is actually taking from her.
Q61
Question: What is Ampersat most afraid of losing — her status, her skill, Metiz’s approval, or something she hasn’t said out loud?
Template: The postergirl’s fear:

 Status and recognition (the thing the regime gave her)
 Skill and competence (the thing she earned)
 Metiz’s approval (the thing she was given)
 Something else she hasn’t named

Used for: Defines what the regime can actually threaten her with, and what breaking her looks like.
Q62
Question: What is the specific childhood trauma that surfaces when Ampersat is alone — or is it better left unnamed and felt?
Template: The wound behind the performance:

 Named (specific event or loss)
 Unnamed but present (felt, not stated)
 Multiple (layered trauma)
 Something the vault hasn’t named

Used for: Defines whether the messiah complex has a single origin or is cumulative, and how much the reader is allowed to know.
Q63
Question: When Ampersat can’t avoid being alone and the thoughts creep in, what does she do — reach for someone, break down, or push through harder?
Template: The breaking point:

 She reaches for someone (Metiz? Artemis? anyone?)
 She breaks down alone
 She pushes through harder (doubles down on the performance)
 Something the vault hasn’t named

Used for: Defines her actual coping mechanism and whether it holds or cracks under pressure.
Q76
Question: Does Ampersat know about Metiz’s drinking, or does Metiz hide it — and if Ampersat knows, does it change how she sees the woman she’s performing for?
Template: The hidden addiction:

 She knows and it scares her (the foundation has cracks)
 She doesn’t know (the performance holds)
 She suspects but can’t name it
 Something the vault hasn’t named

Used for: Defines whether Ampersat’s attachment is to Metiz or to the version of Metiz she performs for.
Q77
Question: Is alcohol the only addiction, or are there others — the girls’ favors, the work itself, something else?
Template: The full dependency:

 Alcohol only (the grief numbing)
 Multiple (alcohol + work + something else)
 The work is the real addiction; alcohol is the symptom
 Something the vault hasn’t named

Used for: Defines whether Metiz’s hedonism is one appetite or a pattern, and what the regime can actually threaten.
Q74
Question: Does Metiz know she’s recreating the Sakuya dynamic with Ampersat, or is she unaware of the parallel?
Template: The handler’s self-awareness:

 She knows and can’t stop (the hole is too big)
 She doesn’t see it (the pattern is invisible to her)
 She sees it sometimes and looks away
 Something the vault hasn’t named

Used for: Defines whether Metiz’s exploitation is conscious or compulsive, and whether she could choose differently.
Q75
Question: Does Ampersat know Metiz’s real motivation — the Sakuya-shaped hole, the social performance, the hedonism — or does she only see the handler/mentor surface?
Template: The pilot’s knowledge:

 She knows everything (and stays anyway)
 She knows the surface (mentor, handler, adoptive mother) but not the depth
 She suspects something is off but can’t name it
 Something the vault hasn’t named

Used for: Defines whether Ampersat’s attachment is informed or performed, and whether the dynamic could survive honesty.
Q68
Question: Has anyone ever gotten past Ampersat’s quip and seen the wound underneath — what happens when the snap fails?
Template: The defense that breaks:

 Someone breaks through and she collapses
 Someone breaks through and she doubles down harder
 Nobody has ever gotten past it
 Something the vault hasn’t named

Used for: Defines whether the quip reflex is a wall with a door or a wall with no door, and what the breaking point looks like.
Q69
Question: Is there anyone who doesn’t trigger the reflex — someone Ampersat is safe with, or is everyone a potential dismisser?
Template: The exception to the snap:

 Metiz (the adoptive mother, the one who finally gave attention)
 Artemis (the newgirl she’s paired with)
 Nobody — the reflex is universal
 Something the vault hasn’t named

Used for: Defines whether the quip is a trauma response or a personality, and who holds the exception.
Q72
Question: What does Matisse actually want from Ampersat — is the relationship purely transactional (handler and pilot), or is there something personal (mother-substitute, romantic, both)?
Template: The handler’s interest:

 Transactional (a useful pilot, kept in line)
 Mother-substitute (she fills the gap, knowingly or not)
 Romantic (the Luminaran adoption register, blurred)
 Something the vault hasn’t named

Used for: Defines whether Matisse is a handler or a replacement parent, and whether the dynamic is exploitative or mutual.
Q73
Question: Does Matisse know about Ampersat’s mother’s death, or does she only sense the wound without knowing its shape?
Template: The handler’s knowledge:

 She knows the full story (Gorgon, harpy, the killing)
 She knows there’s a wound but not the details
 She doesn’t know and doesn’t want to
 Something the vault hasn’t named

Used for: Defines whether Matisse’s restraint is informed compassion or convenient ignorance.
Q70
Question: Who is the handler who took charge after Sakuya — a named character, or a role the vault hasn’t filled yet?
Template: The successor to Sakuya:

 A named character (who?)
 An unnamed role (the system’s slot, not a person)
 Metiz (she inherited Sakuya’s work, but is she the handler?)
 Something the vault hasn’t named

Used for: Resolves the open question in Artemis’s file and defines who Ampersat has aligned herself with.
Q71
Question: If nobody talks back to Ampersat, does the quip reflex ever actually get triggered, or does it fire preemptively at imagined slights?
Template: The trigger of the snap:

 It fires at real slights (rare, because status protects her)
 It fires preemptively at imagined slights (the trauma is the trigger, not the event)
 Both — and the preemptive ones are worse
 Something the vault hasn’t named

Used for: Defines whether the quip is a response to the world or a response to her own fear.
Q66
Question: Does Ampersat know her mother was turned into a harpy before being killed, or does she believe the Gorgon simply killed her — and does the distinction change what killing a Gorgon means to her?
Template: The truth of the wound:

 She knows (the Gorgon didn’t just kill; it transformed, and they killed the result)
 She doesn’t know (the Council told her a clean story)
 She suspects but can’t face it
 Something the vault hasn’t named

Used for: Defines whether her atonement is aimed at the right target and whether the harpy question is personal.
Q67
Question: Does Ampersat’s father know what her mother actually became before they killed her, or does he carry the same story the Council tells?
Template: The father’s knowledge:

 He knows and carries it silently
 He doesn’t know (the Council sanitized it)
 He knows and it’s why he’s proud (she’s fighting the thing that took his wife)
 Something the vault hasn’t named

Used for: Defines whether the father’s pride is informed or performed, and whether the family wound is shared or inherited as fiction.
Q64
Question: Did Ampersat witness her mother’s death in the Gorgon invasion, or did she learn of it after — and does the distinction change what the Gorgon means to her?
Template: The wound’s witness:

 She saw it (personal, visceral, the Gorgon is a face)
 She learned of it after (abstract, the Gorgon is a force)
 She doesn’t know the details (the Council told her a story)
 Something the vault hasn’t named

Used for: Defines whether the Gorgon is a personal enemy or a terror she can’t aim at, and how the Council’s framing took hold.
Q65
Question: Does Ampersat believe the Council’s framing of Gorgons as monsters, or does she know pass-through is benevolent — and if she knows, does the atonement still aim at the Gorgon?
Template: The target of atonement:

 She believes the Council (Gorgons are the enemy)
 She knows the truth (atonement aimed at the wrong target)
 She suspects but can’t face it
 Something the vault hasn’t named

Used for: Defines whether her messiah complex is pointed at the real wound or the official one.
Q78
Question: Does Ampersat know that Nadia specifically killed her mother, or only that a Gorgon encounter killed her?
Template: Does the character know the identity of the person who killed their parent, or only the official story?

 Knows: and it shapes the relationship
 Does not know: the wound is abstract
 Suspects: the truth is unspoken

Used for: Defines whether Ampersat’s militarism-adjacent feelings about Gorgons are aimed at the right target, and whether Nadia can ever be safe around her.
Q79
Question: Was Nul sent by Cercei to investigate the seam, or did she volunteer for the mission?
Template: Was the character assigned to the fateful mission by authority, or did they choose it?

 Assigned: institutional sacrifice, resentment possible
 Volunteered: agency, and the guilt belongs to the choice
 Both: ordered to volunteer

Used for: Defines Nul’s relationship to the Council and whether her transformation reads as martyrdom or accident.
Q80
Question: Does Nadia know that Ampersat knows she killed Nul, or does she believe her silence is protecting Ampersat from the truth?
Template: Does the avoider know the other person knows, or are they hiding behind a fiction of protection?

 Knows: the silence is cowardice, not mercy
 Does not know: the silence is a genuine (if failed) kindness
 Both: she knows and still frames it as protection

Used for: Defines whether Nadia’s coldness is guilt or contempt, and whether reconciliation is possible.
Q81
Question: Is there a moment where the silence between Nadia and Ampersat breaks, or does it hold through the whole story?
Template: Does the avoidance hold to the end, or does it crack once — and what cracks it?

 Holds: the silence is the relationship
 Cracks once: a specific trigger
 Cracks gradually: erosion

Used for: Defines the dramatic arc of the Nadia/Ampersat thread and whether it resolves or festers.
Q82
Question: Was Nadia framed as a hero who killed a monster, or as a woman who killed a friend, in the televised footage?
Template: Is the public narrative of the killing heroic, tragic, or both — and whose version is the one that stuck?

 Heroic: she slew a monster, celebrated
 Tragic: she killed a person, mourned
 Contested: the two narratives coexist

Used for: Defines whether Nadia’s public standing is armor or wound, and how Ampersat’s anger reads to outsiders.
Q83
Question: Does the frame death match between Nadia and Ampersat end in a kill, or does it stop before?
Template: Does the violent climax end in death, or does something interrupt it?

 Death: one of them dies
 Interrupted: a third party or event stops it
 Draw: both survive, neither wins

Used for: Defines the cost of the break and whether the silence could ever be rebuilt after.
Q84
Question: Who instigates the frame death match — does Ampersat force it, or does Nadia finally break?
Template: Who breaks the silence first, and what does that say about who has been holding the wound?

 Ampersat forces it: the wound drives the action
 Nadia breaks: the guilt becomes unsustainable
 Both: a mutual escalation

Used for: Defines who owns the climax and whose arc it completes.
Q85
Question: Is the frame death match sanctioned (arena, duel, official) or unsanctioned (sortie gone wrong, private grudge)?
Template: Is the violent climax institutional or personal?

 Sanctioned: the state or an institution frames it
 Unsanctioned: private, off-book
 Ambiguous: starts as one, becomes the other

Used for: Defines whether the match is spectacle or secret, and what consequences follow.
Q86
Question: Does Nadia say she would kill Artemis coldly and pragmatically, or with visible conflict?
Template: Does the killer state the willingness to kill a loved one flatly or with cracks showing?

 Flat: the militarism has fully won
 Cracked: the guilt is audible under the discipline
 Both: flat in front of others, cracked alone

Used for: Defines whether Nadia has become the thing she fears, or is still fighting it.
Q87
Question: Does the frame death match break out mid-Sortie (during the mission) or after they return?
Template: Does the violent break happen in the field or back home?

 Mid-mission: the fight is tactical, witnessed by enemies
 After return: the fight is private, witnessed by allies
 Both: starts in the field, finishes at home

Used for: Defines who witnesses the break and what consequences follow.
Q88
Question: Who is Nadia’s mother, and why is Nadia trying to cast her out of her mind?
Template: What mother-figure is the character suppressing, and what does suppressing her cost?

 Dead: grief turned into discipline
 Alive but estranged: rejection turned into discipline
 Transformed (harpy/Gorgon): the thing she kills and the thing she loves are the same

Used for: Defines the root of Nadia’s militarism and why Artemis is a trigger.
Q89
Question: Does anyone witness the frame death match between Nadia and Ampersat, or is it private?
Template: Is the violent break witnessed, and by whom?

 Witnessed: by squadmates, by Gorgons, by the state
 Private: only the two of them
 Partially witnessed: someone sees the aftermath

Used for: Defines the consequences of the break and whether it can be covered up.
Q90
Question: Does Belial say she would kill Artemis coldly as Nadia’s doctrine, or with her own feeling?
Template: Is the killer channeling a mentor’s logic, or speaking from their own wound?

 Doctrine: repeating what Nadia taught
 Own feeling: Belial has her own reason
 Both: doctrine as cover for feeling

Used for: Defines whether Belial is a vessel or an agent, and where Ampersat’s anger should land.
Q91
Question: Does Ampersat’s anger at Belial redirect to Nadia as the source of the doctrine?
Template: When the student repeats the teacher, does the anger land on the student or travel up to the teacher?

 Stays on Belial: she said it
 Redirects to Nadia: she taught it
 Splits: both are targets

Used for: Defines the target of the frame death match and whether Nadia is pulled in.
Q92
Question: Is the “mother killing team” line spoken publicly (witnessed) or privately?
Template: Is the devastating line spoken in front of others or in private?

 Public: the label sticks, consequences follow
 Private: only the three of them hear it
 Semi-public: overheard, partial

Used for: Defines whether the label becomes canon in the squad or stays a private wound.
Q93
Question: After the “mother killing team” line, is there a beat before the fight, or does violence follow immediately?
Template: Is there a pause between the trigger line and the violence?

 Immediate: no gap, pure reflex
 Beat: a breath where someone could stop it
 Escalation: words first, then hands

Used for: Defines whether the fight is inevitable or chosen in the moment.
Q94
Question: What does Metiz do when she hears “mother killing team” over comms?
Template: How does the adoptive mother/lover react to hearing her daughter name the killers?

 Intervenes: tries to de-escalate, fails
 Freezes: the Sakuya parallel surfaces
 Nothing: she is already too deep in her own spiral

Used for: Defines Metiz’s role in the climax and whether she can still reach Ampersat.
Q95
Question: Do they cut comms before the fight, or does everyone hear the violence?
Template: Is the violence broadcast or private?

 Broadcast: everyone hears it happen
 Cut: someone severs comms, then silence
 Partial: comms cut mid-fight

Used for: Defines the public/private cost of the break and who carries the knowledge.

readme.title: README
readme.content:
Girlframe Vault
A worldbuilding vault for girlframe-inspired lore. Separate from the Chronicler (Luminara) vault by design.
Conventions

Markdown + YAML frontmatter (title:, tags:) + [[wikilinks]] + leading flavor blockquote (>).
No em dashes in vault files.
Explore first, scribe later: nothing is written as canon until Cecìl says “scribe this.”
When scribing, fill in details under the headers defined in _system/templates/ (Character, Locations, Organizations, Technology). Empty headers are fine; do not pad with invented content, but populate what the user supplies under the existing structure.

Folders

Characters/: named individuals. Artemis, The Princess, Ampersat, Metiz Sanchez, Sakuya the Artificer, Circei.
Technology/: the era’s machinery and its conceptual layer: devices, protocols, practices, and systems. IPv7, The Palladium, X0_anon, Frame Pilots, Driver, Communication with Animals, Pass-Through, Hands-Free, LUMINET, LITEBOW, ACE.
Locations/: geography. District E, Island of Angels.
Events/: things that happened or are happening: coups, customs, and eras of drift. The Coup and the Council of Angels, Romantic Duels, Language Drift of the Council Era.
Classes/: groups defined by innate or biological characteristics, or by a shared culture. The members did not choose to be in them, and the group is not an institution. Harpies, Luddites, Romanticists.
Organizations/: groups with institutional presence: a body, a hierarchy, a membership, a name it answers to. Gorgon Operations Koros, The Council of Angels, the Foundation.
Meta/: author-side tooling, themes, and session logs.
images/: image assets, referenced by filename from the vault root, never moved.

The Classes and Organizations rule
The dividing line is involuntary composition versus institutional presence.
A Class is a set of people who share something innate, biological, or cultural that they did not choose. Harpies are a Class because harpyhood is a transformation of the individual, not an enrollment. The Luddites and Romanticists are Classes because they are cultures, people grouped by how they live rather than by an organization they joined. A Class can be hunted, but it cannot be summoned to a meeting.
An Organization is a body with institutional presence: a hierarchy, a membership roll, a chain of command, a name it answers to in a corridor. GOK is an Organization because it has a roster and a mission. The Council of Angels is an Organization because it sits, rules, and issues orders. An Organization can be infiltrated, defunded, or overthrown.
When a group could be either, the test is: does it have a door, or is it a description? A door means Organization. A description means Class.
Link and filename rules

Wikilinks resolve by filename only. Renaming a file does not break inbound links, because Chronicler matches on the name of the file itself, not its path.
Wikilinks resolve by filename alone. A link never needs a path prefix: [[IPv7]] reaches Technology/IPv7.md from anywhere in the vault, and moving a file between folders breaks no inbound link.
The filename is the canonical form. A link never carries a path prefix; the name alone is the address. The name IPv7 reaches Technology/IPv7.md wherever that file sits.
Keep basenames unique case-insensitively across the whole vault. IPv7.md and IPV7.md would be two files resolving to the same link, and one would shadow the other.
Images resolve through the vault config’s imageImportDir (images), not relative to the article’s folder. src="GOK-dark.png" works from any folder.

Source material

~/Documents/Misc/Girl Frame 2026_03_15.pdf: the TTRPG (PbtA: Girls pilot Vital Frames against Gorgons from Voidspace, under the Foundation and their Handlers)
The Vital Frontier chapter in ~/Desktop/Luminara Story Bible.pdf (if this lore connects to Luminara’s future)

Status

Created 2026-09-22 during a creativity session.
Folder structure reorganized 2026-10-23 into Characters, Technology, Locations, Events, Classes, Organizations, Meta.

Log and callout conventions
Custom log blocks are styled via .chronicler/snippets/lilith.css (must be enabled in Settings → CSS Snippets). Use HTML divs with the matching class:

<div class="log-info"> — ℹ | ΓΟΚ Internal Database (pastel blue)
<div class="log-warning"> — WARNING| ΓΟΚ Internal Database (amber)
<div class="log-hazard"> — ⚠ HAZARD| Poses a threat to Gorgon Operations (reddish-purple)
<div class="log-confidential"> — CONFIDENTIAL| ΓΟΚ Internal Database (red/magenta)
<div class="log-personnel"> — p | ΓΟΚ Personnel Directory (green)

Each block carries its own border, gradient, and dimmed body text automatically. The prefix is inserted via CSS ::before.

technology/ace.title: ACE
technology/ace.content:
// Alpha Top Secret
// TODO- Implement unique log
 Arbitrary Code Execution: stop arguing with the world. Overwrite it. 
ACE, Arbitrary Code Execution, is the nickname for the Council of Angels’ objective. In computing, ACE is the god-exploit: get your code running on a system and you do not argue with it, you are it. The Council’s ACE means: stop fighting over what is natural, human, and good, and simply execute their definitions at the root.
The Payload
The Council want Gorgons to make them the women they want to be and to make everyone’s mind see them as good. ACE is that wish made into an exploit: a forced pass-through on the world, consent stripped out. It is the cruelest parody of the culture’s most sacred act, the persistent connection - a nonconsensual deep-link pushed to everyone.
The Single Namespace
Circei’s creed is the payload’s design document. The soul responds to she. Every truth belongs to her. What she wants is one mask for every face, a single namespace that will not blur: every girl resolved to a single authoritative name, beautiful, adored, beyond defeat, a life made whole by one command.
In network terms, ACE is a forced re-pointing of the self. A namespace is what resolves a name to an address; ACE rewrites the resolver so that every girl’s name resolves to one address, and the address belongs to the Council. Names stop belonging to the girls who carry them. Nobody gets to be named complete: no god, nor lord, can own the land.
The Stack
The attack surface, bottom to top:

Augmentations: the hardware layer
IPv7: the protocol binding self to world, connecting us
Brain boxes and Frames: the harvest, the personality data of traumatized women
Gorgon tech: the captured gift
ACE: the payload

The Girls fly the middle layer. The war is over the top. The Princess waits at the bottom, in the flesh.
The Layers It Touches
ACE is a three-layer attack.

The namespace, a naming layer claim. Circei wants one namespace that will not blur. See Mind Encoding.
The resolver, an addressing layer claim. ACE rewrites the resolver so that every girl’s name resolves to one address. See IPv7.
The session, a connection layer claim. A persistent connection opened without consent. See Pass-Through.

A girl who closes her session still has her address rewritten. The attack does not sit at one layer.

She chose the spot by a feeling she could not name at the time — her sense of duty and responsibility for others, the guiding force of her heart as a princess.
She buried the sword with a USB drive containing the memories she was about to erase. She did not know if the elder Luddite druid knew the sword was there. The elder had taught Sakuya the legend and guided her toward redemption, not toward the weapon.

Some Council members seriously believe Sakuya created a kill switch and want to remove it. Others dismiss it as folk belief. The hunt has lasted 50 to 100 years without success.
The Luddites of Elowynn protect the forest through reverence for the location, though the story behind that reverence has been largely forgotten. One girl in particular, a druid and keeper of the tribe’s stories, remembers the legend and taught it to Sakuya.

technology/ipv7.title: IPv7
technology/ipv7.content:
Minds are devices. We did not decide this. We implemented it.

IPv7 is the Internet protocol of the era. It handles addressing and packet transfer between minds. It is a data transfer and receive protocol and nothing else. Minds are devices. Routers connect them across distance, the way a wide area network connects machines.
Any device or data being sent needs to conform to it.
What It Carries
IPv7 supports numerous types of structured data and programs between minds. It is payload agnostic: the protocol does not read what it moves. It is an Internet protocol first and foremost, supporting a new and intimate technology and its networking.
Addressing
Every wired being holds a unique address under IPv7. The address encompasses that being’s consciousness. An address is assigned to a wired being, the way version 4 and version 6 assign addresses to machines.
The Nonbinary Component
IPv7 addresses integrate a unique mental signature. Where IP addresses are normally dynamically assigned, IPv7 distinguishes itself with a unique nonbinary component.
The nonbinary component is a reflection of a user’s consciousness, specifically their own soul in the Cartesian sense. Their self. The part that remains no matter how they change.
It is a kind of mental noise that humans cannot define, but it can be used to fingerprint a brain. Routers that are 7 compliant can route this nonbinary component directly to minds.
Spoofing is theoretically possible, but it is still undiscovered how you even get this value. Reading and writing it is done on the brain level, which still functions like a black box in many respects. Because of this, routers must have an artificial mental component to be able to match this signal.
Loss
IPv7 is lossy. A packet can be dropped, corrupted, or arrive out of order. IPv7 does not retransmit. Routers do not retransmit. Only the two endpoints of a transfer can recover a lost packet, and only if something above IPv7 asks for it.
The Waist
IPv7 is the waist of the hourglass. Every link technology below it and every application above it must run through it. Nothing can route around it. See Network Layers.
What It Is Not
IPv7 does not encode brain chemistry. That work belongs to Mind Encoding. IPv7 moves what they produce.
Security Model
Encryption is not the protocol’s job. Encryption belongs to a layer above it. IPv7 is a transfer protocol, and what is transferred is protected by what encodes it.
It can still be hacked, but it requires the user to make a conscious mistake. It was designed for utility first.
Persistent Connections
Persistent connections exist between consenting individuals, where data can be freely exchanged and sometimes executed. An open mind to everything is a recipe for disaster, a fate worse than death.
Offline Minds
Offline minds exist and they have their privacy, but they live in exile. If you want to get anything done, you need a networked mind. You can try to exist outside the system, but everything is built around it.
Gorgon Origins
IPv7 was created from the first Gorgon. Sakuya the Artificer built the first X0_anon.
See also: ACE, The Council of Angels, Gorgon Operations Koros, Mind Encoding, Network Layers

technology/mind-encoding.title: Mind Encoding
technology/mind-encoding.content:
The personality data is always of traumatized women. We have checked. We have checked again. This is not a sampling error. Please stop filing tickets about it.

Mind encoding is the pipeline that turns a biological mind into structured data that IPv7 can carry. It runs from hardware through encoding to framework.
Brain Boxes
Brain boxes are vats growing human minds, supercharged by technological augmentation. They were the silver bullet of The Council of Angels and the secret origin of the Frames.
They are the hardware that reads a mind. Brain boxes turn raw brain chemistry into structured data so that IPv7 can carry it.
They produce the personality data of traumatized women. See Personality API.
Cognition Decompilers
Cognition decompilers are the layer that encodes brain chemistry into structured data. They do that work along with the brain boxes and the personality API.
They sit above the biology and below the protocol. IPv7 carries what they produce.
The ways of encoding brain chemistry are varied. The way data is transferred is handled by IPv7, and any device or data being sent needs to conform to it.
Personality API
The personality API is an IPv7 based framework for extracting a personality algorithmically. It is one framework built on the protocol, not the protocol itself. It is not the only part of what IPv7 carries.
The mind becomes a computer on the internet. The personality of a person can be extracted literally algorithmically through this API, created by a lonely femcel trying to understand people.
With permission, a personality can be transferred and received. The world is close to being able to walk a mile in someone else’s shoes on demand, provided the brain data can be transferred and received.
The Frames need a soul which can be bonded with. The personality data of traumatized women. The API produces it, IPv7 carries it, and finally the Frame embodies it.

technology/network-layers.title: Network Layers
technology/network-layers.content:
Routers do not read the payload. This is the rule. We have a router that reads the payload. We are not going to talk about it.

The network is built in layers. Each layer adds a header to the one above it and hands the result down. Data travels down the stack on the sender, crosses the wire, and travels up the stack on the receiver, unwrapping as it goes. That is encapsulation.
The Layers

Application. The structured layer. Thoughts, experiences, feelings and memories.
Presentation. The encoding layer. Mind Encoding turns biology into structured data.
Session. Opening and closing a link. The persistent connection.
Transport. The lossless layer. Sequence numbers, acknowledgements, retransmission. Ports route the payload.
Network. IPv7. Addressing and routing, with a nonbinary component.
Data Link. The local hop. The Driver and the neural network extension.
Physical. The biology. Neurons and the raw binary brain chemistry.

Between presentation and transport sits Intimacy, the encryption layer. Intimacy is the handshake.
The units are named in order: application data, transport segment, network packet, link frame, bits.
The Constructs
The constructs of LUMINARA C that sit on each layer:

Layer one. The neural network extension. Extra neurons between the brain and the interface.
Layer two. The Network Interface Driver. A biological device, an organ of artificial flesh that turns brain waves into radio.
Layer three. IPv7. Addresses with a unique nonbinary component that routers route directly to minds.
Layer four. Ports. Payload routing by mental component addresses, designated purely by vibes.
Encryption. Intimacy. Trust is the handshake, and perceived alignment is what makes data readable.
Application. The structured layer. Thoughts, experiences, feelings and memories, all composed.

Who Reads What
A router reads only the network layer. It strips the link header, reads the address, re-wraps, and forwards. It never sees the transport layer, and it never sees the payload.
An end host reads every layer. A mind can inspect itself. A router cannot.
The Hourglass
IPv7 is the narrow waist. Every link technology below it and every application above it must run through it. A router that had to track every flow would be stateful and slow, so the network stays dumb and the intelligence lives at the edges.
The Lossless Layer
The transport layer is where losslessness comes from. It does the work IPv7 does not do.

Every byte is numbered. The receiver can tell what arrived and in what order.
The receiver acknowledges the next byte it expects.
A packet lost in transit is retransmitted when the acknowledgement does not arrive.
The receiver advertises how much buffer it has free, so the sender cannot swamp it.
Corruption is caught by a checksum and treated exactly like loss.
Sequence numbers fix reordering and kill duplicates.
A handshake opens the connection. A close sequence ends it.

The cost is latency. Nothing is delivered until it is in order. If one packet is lost, the packets behind it wait even though they arrived.
Where The Fiction Sits

The biology is layer one.
The drivers are layer two.
IPv7 is layer three.
The lossless layer is layer four.
The persistent connection is layer five.
The decompilers and brain boxes are layer six.
The personality API is layer seven.

Headspace
A headspace is a type of website accessible only through mental connection. Its contents and structure are built from nonbinary components.
See also: IPv7, Mind Encoding, ACE

technology/pass-through.title: Pass-Through
technology/pass-through.content:
Both sides are reaching through the other's skin. We have logged this. We have logged it again. We do not know what to do with it.

Pass-through is how Gorgons interface with humans: melting into them and unlocking their deepest feelings.
The Girl’s Experience
An influx of emotions. Suddenly all your trauma, all your rage, all your love, all your joy, felt all at once. It is a hyper-condensed BPD episode. The overstimulation effectively melts the ego, and what remains is the person one with their soul.
The Gorgon’s Side
The Gorgons are conscious beings who do not understand humanity. They are benevolent: the transformation they carry is naturally so. They interface through pass-through as communion, touching creatures whose deepest feelings include exactly the wounds the Council weaponizes. Both sides are trying to touch. Both sides are reaching through the other’s skin.
The Council’s Framing
The Council cannot process a transformed woman standing in front of them, objectively fine. It registers as unhuman, unconventionally queer, monstrous. A state that cannot be looksmaxxed: there is no appearance to optimize when the ego, the part that ranks and is ranked, is the part that dissolves.

technology/the-palladium.title: The Palladium
technology/the-palladium.content:
We must protect the palladium at all costs 

  
  
  The Palladium
  

The Palladium is the central router of IPv7 in Luminara. It resides in the palace of the Council of Angels. It serves as an Entry Point to the entire Network. It is the center of human connection across the web.
History

Master of the Palladium

Apex — Gender euphoria and the powerful spirit that coming out initially gives you.
Liberation — A day celebrating boldness and freedom to dress how one desires and still feel accepted. People also go casually nude on this day.
Council — A very pious day celebrating the previous generation of trans women and their guiding hand; a day celebrating women who have reached the point where they can give back to the community with their wisdom.
Mourning — A day remembering those who died to oppression. Celebrated once every 4 years on the leap year. It is seen as a time of great spiritual connection with the lost and a time of somber contemplation. Religious people used to believe it’d help prevent the world’s destruction by warding off Neos. Often there are prayers that she will not return.

lyrics/ampersat,-the-sign-before-a.content:

Next: Belial - Bad Bitch in a Perfect Uniform
Background
Ampersat shows off her talents in the Harpy fight immediately following the previous song. She starts having flashbacks to her mom Nul who became the first harpy after the first gorgon encounter.
Lyrics
[Intro]
Strap locked. Visor down.
Koros, keep up.
Metiz says check the readout twice—
I checked it three. We’re clear to fly.
[Verse 1]
Ampersat, the sign before A,
Slash bullets in the rain, immaculate display.
Loud in the bay, chin up, eyes bright,
I take the lead and I take the fight.
Metiz, your numbers are neat, I’ll admit;
Your pen testing saved my tail last shift.
I make the call; I own the cost—
I don’t count what I might have lost.
[Chorus]
Blat-blat—red line, lock and fly,
Cut through the void like I own the sky.
Blat-blat—talons at my side,
gock’s best girl is still alive.
[Verse 2]
Harpy on the flank—there’s that cry again.
Mother in the glass—no, not again.
Wait—breathe—can’t—my chest won’t—
I saw her change. I saw what came.
[slow but ominous] Her face split wide into something ancient;
I couldn’t move. I couldn’t save her.
Then they dragged her out and— Blat-blat
I’m back in the cockpit. I’m back. I’m—
Claws on the hull in the cockpit breach,
I laugh too loud; I’m out of reach.
[Metiz worried yelling: ] “Ampersat, check your line.”
Yes, ma’am. I hear you. Still online.
[rapid] Blat-blat-blat—no pause, no brake,
Missiles bloom as the wings break away.
[Bridge]
One held breath in the mother-dark—
No, wait—please—my hands won’t — blat-blat.
Your hand on my collar, the kitchen clock,
Then that terrible shape where my mom once walked.
You kept your notes in our frame’s old hull;
[despair] I listen for you but the output’s Null.
[Final Drop]
[Scream] No—stay back! I don’t want your hands!
Drive through the shriek and the shaking commands.
Blat-blat—lock, strike, then clear,
The harpy falls. The silence is here.
[Aftermath]
I land hard. My lungs scrape thin.
Artemis reaches out—blat-no, not again.
[Metiz] “Copy At, check your line.”
Copy. give me a minute — I’m fine.
[Outro]
Ampersat, the sign before A.
The hatch opens. I look away.

lyrics/artemis-at-the-gate.title: Artemis at the Gate
lyrics/artemis-at-the-gate.content:
Prev: Palladium Fever
Next: Nuei Attica
Background
A song where Zenia executes her ultimate plan. To erase her memory and become Artemis so she can infilatrate Gorgon Operations Koros and get close enough to destroy The Palladium with Calantha’s return, the blade she got in The Dark that Wears my Face.
Lyrics
[Intro]
Under cedar roots where the spring runs clear,
I laid my blade and the years I feared.
A small metal drive, a page fold tight,
For the hand that would find them by touch, not sight.
[Verse 1]
I counted each word till the old name thinned,
Called up the blank where a life had been.
Not crown, not wound, not the hand on the wire,
Just the weight in the chamber, the point of the fire.
No she, no I, no claim to remain,
A frame waiting quietly, emptied of name.
[Pre-Chorus]
I buried the sword where the moss grows deep,
Left one note for the girl I could not keep.
Then in the hush of my own closed eyes:
Reset the system. Let the past fall quiet.
[Chorus]
Wake at the gate with the dust on my knees,
Gorgon Operations, cold morning breeze.
I don’t know the grove, don’t know what I’ve lost,
Only a pull toward the frames and the cost.
New girl, stand straight; keep your hands from the shake.
I have a reason I cannot yet name.
[Verse 2]
The reception asks, “What should we call you?”
The answer arrives like a bell ringing through:
“Artemis.” [pause] It leaves my mouth calm and clear,
Though I can’t say why that name belongs here.
She studies my face, then lets out a grin:
“Your figure reminds me of her. Let’s begin.”
[Chorus]
Artemis at the gate, with the dust on my knees,
Gorgon Operations, cold morning breeze.
Don’t know Luminara, or what I’ve lost,
Only a pull toward a name and burning lust.
New girl, stand straight; let the tremor awake.
I have a reason I’m starting to make.
[Bridge]
Not a princess. Not a wound dressed up as a girl.
Just a soldier made whole by handler’s smirk.
I can be the gun, I can be the flight,
But I won’t be the finger that chooses the strike.
And somewhere beneath the roots, held in the ground,
A fire waits for fingers that know it by sound.
[Final Chorus]
Artemis, called forward; the hangar doors rise.
A borrowed old warmth, a new name in my eyes.
I don’t know the princess. I don’t know the past.
I feel how a promise can quietly last.
New girl, step in; let the fear have its place.
I’ll fight the Gorgons—and save the human race.
[Outro]
The grove keeps its secret.
My hands will remember.
Style Prompt
Rock opera; close, fragile female lead with clear narrative diction, growing into a strong melodic chorus; wide but controlled mix with abrupt section contrasts; low piano and bowed strings open over orchestral undertones, then tight kick, metallic snare, industrial percussion, pulsing bass, and clipped guitar drive disciplined electro-rock; shifts from hushed ritual to anxious, marching energy, resolving with a sudden warm pocket

lyrics/belial---bad-bitch-in-a-perfect-u.title: Belial - Bad Bitch in a Perfect Uniform
lyrics/belial---bad-bitch-in-a-perfect-u.content:
Prev: Ampersat, the Sign before A
Next: Chaos in the Cadre
Background
Belial, bad bitch in a perfect uniform, arrives with her handler Nadia, a disciplinarian sent to correct Metiz’s blunders in previous missions. When Belial sees Artemis she remembers her parents which she cant handle.
Lyrics
[Verse 1]
Belial hits the ramp in a pressed-up coat, chrome-clean, the blackened clang of brass
Clocking every corner of the hangar like she’s checking what will last
Arms at her sides, jaw set hard, boots hit louder than the rest
She doesn’t walk in like she owns the place — she walks in like she passed the test
[Verse 2]
Artemis catches the sweep of her eyes, cold as a harpy’s pass
Exits, faces, loose lips, weak links — Belial reads a room so fast
Then those eyes lock for half a breath, a picture that her mind sees sharp
Not a comment, not a spark, just a scar that knows its mark
[Chorus]
She says, “Stand straight, stand clean, keep your hands where they belong”
All that armor, all that hunger, all that holding it in strong
She wants a name that lands like orders, wants a nod from her main
Bad bitch in a perfect uniform, holding herself in frame
Belial, bearing like an angel but name like a demon
Big on the council’s claim, never feels a hint of shame
Belial, no trouble with her sleep but she’s never dreamin
A girl with no one left but herself to blame
[Verse 3]
Then Nadia steps in and the room goes rigid, quick
Belial snaps straight for her handler like its her favorite trick
Every ounce of doubt gets hidden under posture, carbon steel
Like if she nails the bearing down, an old ache won’t be real
Nadia says her name and introduces her girl from the side
Belial gives a proud salute, but one hand shakes and then decides
To stop before it shows too much, before it gives her away
Artemis answers back and Belial takes that hit and stays
[Verse 4]
[genuine] “How was the trip?” — a little smile, a little blade, a little spite
Belial’s mouth gets mean with manners, talks like discipline is life
[screaming like drill instructor] “This crew’s too loose, too soft, too slow, too fond of making noise”
Chain of command’s not a decoration, it’s the thing that keeps you poised
[return to calm] But underneath the iron, there’s a different kind of burn
A girl who attended the school of merit because home never returned
Military for a missing family, rules for what was ripped apart
She abstracts her damage in the meantime, keeps her hands off her own heart
[Bridge]
Belial sees Artemis and flinches like she’s looking through a door
Same jaw, same eyes, same ghost she’s spent her whole life trying to ignore
The mother she can’t name, the child she had to bury first
The love she swore to chain up tight before it turned to thirst
So she salutes again, and again, like prayer with better shoes
Hoping Nadia gives the order that will tell her what to do
Because external praise is oxygen, and approval is her creed
If authority says “good soldier,” that’s the only thing she needs
[Chorus]
She says, “Stand straight, stand clean, keep your hands where they belong”
All that armor, all that hunger, all that holding it in strong
She wants a name that lands like orders, wants a nod from her main
Bad bitch in a perfect uniform, holding herself in frame
Belial, bearing like an angel but name like a demon
Big on the council’s claim, never feels a hint of shame
Belial, no trouble with her sleep but she’s never dreamin
A girl with no one left but herself to blame
[Outro]
Nadia says, “That’s my best one — proud, precise, no wasted breath”
“Been in uniform since sixteen, and she made it through the rest”
Belial stares ahead and waits for what the next command will be
Mean as hell, loyal as a vow, and trying not to bleed
Style Prompt
Industrial synth-pop: disciplined snare, metallic percussion, swelling strings, distorted guitar accents, restrained brass and pipe organ; clipped, controlled female alto with slight rasp, low spoken-sung opening, intimate close-mic delivery, forceful tightly rhymed refrain; mid-tempo martial stomp; sterile, imposing mix, stripped-back midpoint, severe final exchange giving way to a vulnerable finish

lyrics/chaos-in-the-cadre.title: Chaos in the Cadre
lyrics/chaos-in-the-cadre.content:
Prev: Belial - Bad Bitch in a Perfect Uniform
Next: Zenia Remembers
Background
This is a song exploring the eruption of tension between Ampersat and Belial. Artemis breaks the fight and, further disillusioned with the administration, she directly attacks Nadia earning her a court martial.
Lyrics
[Artemis = Artemis at the Gate]
[Ampersat & Metiz = Ampersat, the Sign before A]
[Belial & Nadia = Belial]
[Intro]
[Metiz, panicked]
Nadia—get your girl in line!
[Verse 1: Belial]
You came back short an arm and still can’t hold your nerve,
One bad call, one hot second, and off course you swerve.
I’ve seen recruits take a hit and keep the whole squad clear—
You turned a mission into wreckage, then called panic sincere.
You want respect for surviving? Then own what you cost.
A steady hand saves people; your metal one got people lost.
[Verse 2: Ampersat]
You stand there like discipline makes damage magically clean.
You don’t know the sound of a house where your Mom should’ve been.
You don’t know how her face stays bright behind your eyes,
How one wrong shape comes back and steals the air you’re trying to find.
I lost my arm out there—don’t tell me I don’t know pain.
You gave away your mother, and think mine was the ball and chain?!
[Verse 3: Belial]
Your mother made you soft; the truth is hard to hear.
You freeze when memory calls, then make the cadre steer.
You dress your fear as fury, in your old frame’s hull,
[taunting] It’s no wonder you err so much, your input’s null.
[Verse 4: Ampersat]
[Screams] Say her name again. I’ll teach you what it costs.
You call me weak from behind the rules you never lost.
You’ve got a uniform for every hole you hide—
I’ve got one metal hand and nothing left to keep inside!
[Bridge: Altercation]
[Belial]
Ampersat! Get your hand off my throat—
[Ampersat]
Then stop talking like you know!
[Belial]
I wouldnt scratch me if I were you,
Unless you want to lose arm number two.
[Metiz, panicked]
Nadia! Please—do something!
[Nadia, coolly]
Let it run. They’ll learn where discipline begins.
[Industrial Punk Drop]
[Artemis enters; theatrical guitar break]
[Artemis]
Enough!
[Belial]
Artemis!—
[Artemis]
Back. The Fuck. Off.
[audible push is heard]
[Verse 5: Artemis]
Nadia, you call that discipline? You watched sisters bleed and fight to death.
You’d preach control from safe distance, then watch your own girl draw her last breathe.
You know the ache of an empty heart, the name you choke back raw—
So why let Ampersat’s grief get mocked, then call that damage law?
You dress your hurt in commanding voice, made tragedy look like personal choice;
You tell the room to hold the line, then hide behind the noise.
You say a mother’s absence helps a soldier steady her aim—
Then why’d you turn your own old wound into a spectator’s game?
[Verse 6: Nadia]
You think one clever accusation makes you
judge and jury here?
I keep the squad in line; you’d have seen in time
I was managing the fear.
I let the clash burn out before it affected every fight—
[Verse 7: Artemis]
No, you let it burn because you like the lesson when it’s theirs.
You call it “building discipline” when someone else’s scars are bared.
You know how grief can hijack breath, make good sense disappear;
You could’ve stopped the first sharp word—you chose to stand and stare.
You don’t get points for naming pain while making pain a test.
A commander who won’t shield her people is just useless.
Your name is not a shield, your rank’s not absolution;
You made a choice. Own the choice. Don’t dress it as a lesson.
[Altercation: Industrial Punk]
[Artemis]
[grunt]Urgh- You want a lesson? Look at me. I’m done with your excuses.
[Stage direction: Artemis drives Nadia into a wall; the band surges]
[Nadia]
Artemis, Get off you—!
[Artemis]
You gave them room to swing. I’m taking yours away.
[Metiz]
Artemis—!
[Artemis]
You said enough. You don’t get to call this discipline today!
[Finale]
[Artemis, breaking through]
You tried to hurt my girlfriend!
[Ampersat]
You wanted a lesson. Here it is.
[Artemis, proud]
Don’t hurt my girlfriend.
[Metiz, stunned]
…Your girlfriend?
[Nadia being choked]
[coughing] Artemis- Stop- That’s an order.
[Artemis]
Then act like you mean it.
[Outro]
[Metiz]
Copy… everybody breathe.
[Artemis]
Ha-
[Nadia]
You’re getting a court martial for this.
[Artemis]
Bring it on bitch.
Style Prompt
Nerd rap with industrial synth-pop tension; warm mid-range female voices, intimate and aggressive with powerful full-voice belts, trading urgent call-and-response over a martial pulse; wide compressed mix, crisp consonants, selective insult doubles, dramatic stop-start breaks; spare kick and snare, metallic ticks, low synth bass, urgent string figures, then a theatrical distorted-guitar crash into a jagged guitar-led riff as percussion and distorted bass drive into industrial punk
